blindSummary: No criminalisation of trans presence. This state/province's legislature passed a 2024 reform amending the civil code to create an administrative legal gender recognition procedure, and also recognises the transfemicide offence. No dedicated incident, enforcement or ordinance evidence was found, so there are no local visitor-facing risk signals beyond the country's documented position.
blindSourceSummaries: A major human-rights organisation's state-by-state tracker on legal gender recognition (March 2025), covering which of the country's 32 states/provinces have legislated an administrative procedure and the highest court rulings that drove expansion. For this unit: a 2024 civil-code reform created an administrative legal gender recognition procedure.

A major human-rights organisation's report (6 March 2024) on a neighbouring state/province: the absence of a legal gender recognition procedure there exposes trans people to institutional maltreatment - the August 2023 killing of a trans activist remained unsolved, hate-motivation provisions are absent from that state/province's criminal code, and healthcare staff routinely out patients by calling legal names. A baseline for how a non-reforming state/province behaves.

A major newspaper report (24 July 2024) on the national capital district making transfemicide a crime with sentences up to 70 years (approved 18 July 2024), in one of the deadliest settings for trans people in the region; over 95% of homicides nationally went unpunished in 2022.
blindLocalsOnly: The 2024 legal gender recognition reform and transfemicide-offence recognition are resident-facing civil-registry and criminal-law machinery.
